event.summary: Sidebar retirement can suppress the terminal after a successful Restart
event.detail: Reviewed commits: b3d6b3eff6b7508e0b1fb6ec5b5cde31d27ebabe (new sidebar retirement interacting with this group's changed view/test) and f560058da19e02716e6f943883a9508b447aff4e (removes its generation floor while preserving the surface bug). TLDR: Restart can succeed while its session still shows the interrupted-session card and offers Restart instead of displaying the running agent. A sidebar response can consume the success before the session view uses it to mount the terminal. Details: the prior l1 proposed drop is retracted: a surviving remount-generation increment is insufficient when the terminal surface itself is conditional. At b3d6b3e, session_view.rs:559-564 sets relaunched only from state.restart.filter(succeeded), then advances mount_generation regardless; :3711-3732 returns Interrupted/false for an Interrupted current detail with relaunched=false. list/view.rs:1798 now retires the shared payload from a sidebar listing independently of that current detail. session_ops.rs:92-106 admits any post-floor, nonpending read satisfying stale || status!=Interrupted, and :219-233 erases the payload. Consequently a qualifying newer sidebar response before queued observer effects can remove the success without updating the session view's own Interrupted status. f560058 exposes a stronger pre-Restart-response route: (1) a sidebar read snapshots a stale Interrupted session; (2) the independently read session detail becomes fresh Interrupted and the header admits Restart (session_view.rs:982-1044, :2178-2187); (3) the POST succeeds, list/view.rs:3416-3419 sets restart_succeeded and ends the request without fencing listing_reads; (4) the old successful sidebar reply arrives before any newer listing success and before the view's observer effect. accepts_listing (:756-769) uses ReadGate.accept_success, which compares against applied, not newest started (ops.rs:182-187), so the refresh requested on completion does not itself reject that old response. session_ops.rs:79-80 treats stale=true as confirming, :91-105 requires only no pending request and a true flag, and :215-224 clears success; f560058 removed b3d6b3e's restart_listing_floor. (5) session_view.rs:549-563 sees the changed restart_revision but false success, never sets relaunched, and :1709-1710 supplies an empty terminal specification because :3701-3721 still rejects fresh Interrupted. This is absence of a terminal, not merely a missed generation update. The existing test at b3d6b3e session_view.rs:3955-4015 / f560058 :3912-3960 explicitly permits completion payload retirement before observer effects, but asserts only generation and never observes relaunched or keep_terminal_surface. Contract: b3d6b3e SPEC_impl.md:1133-1138 and f560058 :1134-1140 require that Restart completion reattach the terminal and that a mounted view observe it; SPEC.md Session view requires the real live TUI. Suggested fix direction: preserve completion success independently of retention for future mounts, or let sidebar retirement retire only the future-mount seed while each mounted view consumes its own completion; maintain a read/lifecycle floor for stale pre-Restart replies. Suggested bucket: high, because a successful recovery can leave the terminal unavailable and still invite recovery actions, particularly while the next detail/status read is slow. Confidence: confirmed by source/contract analysis; no execution or reproduction. proposed_drop: false. Could-be-highest: no established security or irreversible work-loss consequence; no claim that another click kills the running agent. possible_cover: parent-supplied g036/l1, g037/f3, g038/l1 and g089/l1 are likely the same interaction; no coverage source inspected. Recovery and limits: session_view.rs:1475-1487 still requests a post-boundary detail read, and :1082-1115 retries failed reads. A later current detail with a non-Interrupted status repairs the surface. A Restart reply alone need not yield that status: helm session_cache.rs:143-146 retains the previous Interrupted status when incoming status is Unknown until an actual host refresh supplies a definite status. Neither sidebar retirement nor mount_generation copies its newer row into this view's current state; :1257-1262 follows only title. Thus the residual is real but not claimed permanent, with duration determined by independent status/detail progress. The b3 route requires a qualifying newer listing before effects; the stale old-response route specifically appears after f560058 removes the floor. Readily checkable premises resolved; no open source lead remains.

event.summary: A discarded header Delete handoff loses the refusal reason
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 2ef10815f12ed719ab6c51c6e3ac6fcd3f8bc1fa. TLDR: when Delete cannot ask the environment's Farhelm, navigating away between its reply and the follow-up question can leave the session undeleted with no explanation of the failure. Details: list/view.rs:3022-3034 first releases the Delete's session claim, then chooses HeaderQuestion if selected still names its source. :3052-3054 removes that source's persistent error and publishes only its ID to warned_delete; the failure branch's ordinary Error alternative at :3056-3057 otherwise records the reason. The new SessionView effect at :784-793 clears warned_delete before checking either that it names this view or that lifecycle.claim_guard succeeds. If navigation changes the keyed view before that effect consumes it, the newly mounted view clears the mismatched handoff and does nothing; if the source acquired a new claim in that interval, the same-view effect likewise consumes without opening. No refusal reason is carried in the handoff (session_ops.rs:135-141), so neither discarded case can reconstruct the deleted error. Cancelling a late question is appropriate; discarding the failed operation's only explanation is the defect. Original suspected consequence retained: Delete changes nothing and silently loses both its warned follow-up and refusal feedback; no unauthorized deletion is alleged. The new effect's exact comment :781-783 deliberately drops a handover for a gone view so it cannot pop up later, but neither that comment nor the product contract authorizes erasing its failure reason.
